reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh's empathy for the people as a whole, not merely for leaders. Although Yahweh punishes the Israelites for their disobedience (delivering them to Philistine rule for 40 years), the narrative immediately pivots to Yahweh providing salvation through a deliverer. The angel announces that the promised son will 'begin to save Israel from the hand of the Philistines' (וְהוּא יָחֵל לְהוֹשִׁיעַ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיַּד פְּלִשְׁתִּים), and the text repeatedly shows Yahweh empowering Samson through His Spirit (ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה) to accomplish victories against the Philistines on behalf of the people. Furthermore, Samson is not portrayed as a traditional leader but rather as a judge and deliverer for the entire nation. The arc of the narrative—judgment followed by provision of a deliverer—demonstrates Yahweh's ultimate care and empathy for the suffering people, not indifference to them.
